dish: Edomae nigiri sushi from master Taichi Tamura's counter
n: Meguro Sushi Taichi (目黒 鮨 太一)
w: A Michelin Bib Gourmand sushi counter in residential Meguro run by master sushi chef Taichi Tamura with his wife — family-oriented, good-value Edomae sushi.

n: Teuchisobadokoro Shisen-an (手打蕎麦処 紫仙庵)
w: A Michelin Bib Gourmand hand-made soba shop tucked into a residential street some distance from Meguro Station.

dish: Hanetsuki ('winged') gyoza and sui-gyoza boiled dumplings
n: Hoanyon (Kangei Honten), Kamata (歓迎 本店)
address: Kamata, Ōta-ku, Tokyo (near JR Kamata Station)
w: One of the three Kamata gyoza houses of the Yagi siblings, the family behind Kamata's hanetsuki (winged) gyoza — the ward's signature dish since 1983; Time Out calls it Kamata's most homely Chinese restaurant.

dish: Pan-fried gyoza — the only dish on the menu, 5 per plate, two-plate minimum
n: Kameido Gyoza Honten (亀戸餃子 本店)
w: A no-frills gyoza hall serving nothing but crisp pan-fried dumplings since 1955; plates keep coming until you say stop. Tokyo Weekender asks whether it is the best gyoza in Tokyo.

dish: Hand-dripped coffee and the no-bake cheesecake certified as a 'Sumida Modern' dessert
w: A traditional kissaten by Hikifune Station where owner Yasutaka Inaba hand-drips every cup; a Love Tokyo Award winner (2017) and a neighbourhood fixture.

dish: Espresso (pulled only until 2pm) and the 'Flower' cortado
n: Bear Pond Espresso, Shimokitazawa (ベアポンド エスプレッソ)
w: Katsu Tanaka's tiny espresso bar in a former sweet shop, open since 2009 and long called Tokyo's coffee mecca; strict house rules — no photos, no laptops, espresso only until 2pm.

dish: Tempura teishoku fried to order at the counter
n: Tempura Shinjuku Tsunahachi (天ぷら 新宿つな八 総本店)
w: Flagship of the tempura house founded in 1923; the Shinjuku shop (1964) was a haunt of kabuki actors and ballplayers and still fries to order at the counter at mid-range prices.

dish: French onion soup, fish quenelle, duck confit and steak frites
w: A Bib Gourmand French bistro (2026 MICHELIN Guide) whose name means 'behind' — it sits behind a two-star restaurant; regional French classics at Asakusa prices.
